questions.question: A motorcycle's brake light is:

options.text: More noticeable than a car's brake light.
Less noticeable than a car's brake light.
Less important than a car's brake light.
Easier to see than a car's brake light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Less noticeable than a car's brake light.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's brake light is not as easy to see as a car's brake light. Flash your brake light before you slow down or stop. This helps other drivers notice that you are braking.

questions.question: Where should you find information about your motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Use your owner's manual as your main source for information about your motorcycle. It tells you how to operate it, how to maintain it, and its specifications.

questions.question: When should you do a pre-ride inspection?
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride. Small problems on a motorcycle are more dangerous than on a car. A pre-ride inspection helps prevent accidents.

questions.question: What kind of shoes should you wear when riding?

options.text: Shoes with long laces that hang out.

questions.explanation: Wear boots or high, sturdy shoes that cover and support your ankles. Use short heels so they don't catch on anything. Tuck in laces so they don't get caught in the motorcycle.

questions.question: How should you ride on a bridge grating?

options.text: Always stay on the far right side of the lane.
Always stay on the far left side of the lane.
Stay relaxed, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay relaxed, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Bridge gratings may cause your motorcycle to sway. This is usually not dangerous. Stay relaxed and ride straight at a steady speed. Do not zigzag to try to stop the sway, as this is dangerous.

questions.question: Low-speed crashes on a motorcycle:

options.text: Happen often, so you don't need to worry.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen at speeds under 30 miles per hour. Even low-speed crashes can be fatal.

questions.question: A face shield:

options.text: Does not protect your face as well as goggles.

questions.explanation: A plastic, impact-resistant face shield gives the best protection for your eyes and face. Regular glasses or sunglasses are not enough. In Vermont, you do not need eye or face protection if your motorcycle has a windshield, but it is still recommended.

questions.question: When is it a good idea to wear reflective clothing?
questions.explanation: Always wear reflective or brightly colored clothing when riding. Crashes happen at any time of day, so wear highly visible clothing whenever you ride.

questions.question: What should motorcycle riding clothes cover?

options.text: Your arms completely, but not your legs.
Your legs completely, but not your arms.
Whatever feels comfortable, safety does not matter.

questions.explanation: For proper protection, wear a jacket and pants that fully cover your arms and legs.

questions.question: Motorcycle signals are:

options.text: More important than signals on larger vehicles.
Only needed when another vehicle is next to you.
Less important than signals on larger vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: More important than signals on larger vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcyclists are more vulnerable than car and truck drivers. This makes proper signaling even more important for motorcycles than for larger vehicles.

questions.question: What is a danger of riding next to parked cars?

options.text: You may not find a parking spot.
A driver may suddenly pull out into your path.
Other drivers may drive slowly while looking for parking.
The road surface may be uneven.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver may suddenly pull out into your path.
questions.explanation: Riding next to parked cars is dangerous. A driver might pull out without looking and hit you. Car doors may open into your lane. Pedestrians may step out between cars.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, what should you do?

options.text: Ride on the shoulder away from traffic.

questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use both brakes when needed, slow down, and avoid sudden movements. Watch for oil, shade, dirt, gravel, and bridges—these have less traction.

questions.question: Shifting to a lower gear is similar to:
questions.explanation: Shifting your motorcycle to a lower gear works like applying the brakes. This is called engine braking.

questions.question: For the best protection, wear a helmet certified by:
questions.explanation: Use a motorcycle helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards for the best protection.

questions.question: How does riding with a passenger affect your motorcycle?

options.text: It usually makes no difference in how it handles.
It is usually safe for beginning riders.
It can change how the motorcycle handles.
It helps new riders learn different riding situations.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can change how the motorcycle handles.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle, which changes how it handles. Only experienced riders should carry passengers.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: What is one benefit of doing regular maintenance on your motorcycle?

options.text: Your motorcycle will run well for a long time.
Maintenance checks can help avoid parking tickets.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your motorcycle will run well for a long time.
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle will continue to run like new if you maintain it properly and do regular inspections.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, you should:

options.text: Prepare and adjust your motorcycle for the passenger.
Ride the same way as without a passenger.
Make sure footrests are only for you.
Teach the passenger how to ride after you start.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prepare and adjust your motorcycle for the passenger.
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle must be properly equipped and adjusted to carry a passenger. It should have separate footrests for the passenger and a large enough seat for two people. You may need to adjust the headlight, tire pressure, and suspension for the extra weight.

questions.question: How should a motorcyclist choose their lane position?

options.text: Pick one spot in the lane and always stay there.
Move around the lane to keep other drivers out.
Choose your position based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Choose your position based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: There is no one best lane position. Change your position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, what must you do?

options.text: You may ride on the shoulder.
You may finish the pass in a no passing zone.
You must start and finish the pass in a passing zone.
You should honk to make the other driver slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must start and finish the pass in a passing zone.
questions.explanation: All passes must be completed within speed limits and only where passing is safe and legal.

questions.question: Where should you find information about your specific motorcycle?

options.text: Someone who rides a different motorcycle.
A television show about motorcycle riding.

questions.explanation: Read your motorcycle's owner's manual before riding it for the first time. This is especially important if you are riding a borrowed motorcycle. The manual tells you how your specific bike works.

questions.question: Who is most likely to be in a motorcycle crash?

options.text: Those who have completed a safety course.

questions.explanation: Crashes happen most often to new riders who have not been trained and who do not know their motorcycle well.

questions.question: What is required for motorcycle passengers to wear?

options.text: Required only when riding with an operator who has had their license for two years or less.
Required only when riding with an operator who had a traffic ticket within the last two years.

questions.explanation: In North Carolina, all riders and passengers must wear helmets. The helmet must meet DOT safety standards.

questions.question: Which surface is NOT slippery?

options.text: A strip of oil in the center of a lane

questions.explanation: Many surfaces are slippery and unsafe for motorcycles. These include wet roads, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, oil, and metal covers. Dry pavement is the safest surface for tires.

questions.question: How do you control the accelerator on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: The accelerator is on the right handgrip. You control it by twisting the grip with your right hand.
